entries.title: Joshua 11:1
segments: Hazor; a strong and chief city in the north part of Canaan.

Madon; not far from Hazor. 
 
  Shimron; called,

, Shimron-meron.  It was afterwards in the tribe of Zebulun. 
 
  Achshaph; west of Zebulun, in the tribe of Asher. 
 
The wicked in their distress often pursue courses which, instead of relieving them, hasten their destruction.

entries.title: Joshua 11:2
segments:
The mountains; probably the mountains of Naphtali north-west of the sea of Tiberias. 
 
  Chinneroth; on the lake of Gennesareth, or sea of Tiberias. 
 
  Dor; on the Mediterranean, not far from mount Carmel.

entries.title: Joshua 11:3
segments: Hermon;
Mizpeh; called,
, "the valley of Mizpeh eastward." Hermon, under which it lay, was in the eastern range of Lebanon.

entries.title: Joshua 11:5
segments: The waters of Merom; a collection of waters in the upper part of Canaan, from which flows the river Jordan.  It is about twelve miles above the sea of Galilee, and is about five miles long, with a level region north of it partially overflowed in the spring.  Its present name is Bahr-el-Huleh.

entries.title: Joshua 11:6
segments:
Hough their horses; hamstring them; cut the great cord of their hind legs. 
 
However numerous the enemies within and without, or however mighty the combinations against the people of God, if in obedience to him they rightly use the means which he gives them, they have no reason to fear, for at which he gives them, they have no reson to fear, for at his appointed time he will cause them to triumph over all their foes.

entries.title: Joshua 11:7
segments: The aid which God gives is not designed to supersede or render needless human efforts; but to encourage men to make efforts, and to render them successful.

entries.title: Joshua 11:8
segments:
Great Zidon; a city on the Mediterranean, about twenty-five miles north of Tyre, fifty south of Beyroot, and sixty-six west of Damascus. It is called great on account of its numerous people and abundant wealth. 
 
  Misrephoth-maim; north of Zidon.

entries.title: Joshua 11:9
segments: The whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain.  Even the brute creation suffer in consequence of the sins of men.  Though these sufferings are under the direction of an infinitely wise, holy, and benevolent God, they are the effects of sin, and a just expression of his indignation against it.

entries.title: Joshua 11:11
segments: Men are often called to most self-denying duties, and those from which the most wise, holy, and benevolent minds would, if consistent, gladly be excused.

entries.title: Joshua 11:12
segments: As Moses--commanded; this is often mentioned to show that for destroying the Canaanites the Israelites were not to be blamed but commended, because that in doing it they were obeying God.

entries.title: Joshua 11:13
segments: Stood still in their strength; rather, "stood upon their hill."  It was the custom to build cities on them.  These cities the Israelites, after destroying their inhabitants, reserved for their own use.

entries.title: Joshua 11:15
segments: Resolute, determined, and habitual obedience to God's commands, is the only course of wisdom, safety, usefulness, and bliss.

entries.title: Joshua 11:16
segments:
The hills; the mountainous region of the south. 
 
  The land of Goshen; see note to

. 
 
  The valley; the low regin bordering on the Mediterranean. 
 
  The plain; the long narrow vale through which the Jordan flows and in which the Dead sea lies.  The southern portion of it opposite to "the south country" is meant.

entries.title: Joshua 11:17
segments: The mount Halak; that is, "the bald mountain."  The writer probably means a line of naked chalk hills running across the valley from the west to east about eight miles south of the Dead sea; the same as "the ascent of Akrabbim," which formed the southern boundary of Canaan.
Mount Hermon; the southern part of Anti-Lebanon.

entries.title: Joshua 11:18
segments:
A long time; about seven years. 
 
We must not cease in our efforts to conquer the spiritual enemies of God and our own souls, till they are so effectually subdued as never again to rise up against us.

entries.title: Joshua 11:20
segments: To harden their hearts; by leaving them, as a punishment for their sins, to pursue their own chosen way to ruin.
When God has determined to destroy men, he lets them pursue their chosen way of folly and sin to their ruin.

entries.title: Joshua 11:21
segments: Hebron--Debir--Anab; in the southern part of the country.

entries.title: Joshua 11:22
segments: Gaza--Gath--Ashdod; cities of the Philistines in the south-west part of Palestine, and near the Mediterranean.

entries.title: Joshua 11:23
segments: Took the whole land; not absolutely every city and region of it, for there remained yet very much land to be possessed,

; but he conquered the whole country so as to be able to divide it by lot to the Israelites. 
 
Perseverance in humble, hearty, courageous obedience to God, will end in sure and most glorious triumph.
